original.title: NIP2 implies almost strongly quadratically atomicity
original.statement: Let an **elementary $p$-group property** (epGP) be a property of elementary abelian $p$-groups, and let $\mathrm{NIP}_2$ denote the stated second-order independence-property condition. An epGP is **almost strongly quadratically atomic** when the required high-rank quadratic factors have bounded complexity and provide the stated approximate atomic decomposition. **NIP2 atomicity conjecture.** If an epGP is $\mathrm{NIP}_2$, then it is almost strongly quadratically atomic. This strengthens the preceding structural result from almost quadratic atomicity to its strong variant; the supplied text gives no resolution.
original.source_name: C. Terry and J. Wolf, “Higher-order generalizations of stability and arithmetic regularity”, arXiv:2111.01739 (2025).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01739

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021). “These important open questions notwithstanding, it is natural to imagine higher-order generalizations of the work presented in this paper.”

original.title: NFOP2 properties are quadratic-atomic or contain a generalized Green–Sanders example
original.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be an elementary $p$-group property, and let $\mathrm{NFOP}_2$ mean that it has no functional order property of order two. A property is **quadratically atomic** when it satisfies the paper's quadratic atomicity condition, and it **contains a generalized Green–Sanders example** when it contains one of the stated generalized obstructions. **NFOP2 dichotomy conjecture.** If an epGP $\mathcal{P}$ is $\mathrm{NFOP}_2$, then it is either quadratically atomic or contains a generalized Green–Sanders example. This is proposed because the Green–Sanders example is $\mathrm{NFOP}_2$ but not quadratically atomic; the conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
original.source_name: C. Terry and J. Wolf, “Higher-order generalizations of stability and arithmetic regularity”, arXiv:2111.01739 (2025).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01739

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021). “These important open questions notwithstanding, it is natural to imagine higher-order generalizations of the work presented in this paper.”

original.title: Bollobás–Nikiforov signless Laplacian conjecture for clique-free graphs
original.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph containing no copy of $K_{r+1}$, and let $m$ be its number of edges. Write $q(G)$ for the signless Laplacian spectral radius. **Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture.** One has

$$
q(G)\le \sqrt{8m\left(1-\frac{1}{r}\right)}.
$$

This is the signless Laplacian analogue of the corresponding adjacency spectral-radius bound for $K_{r+1}$-free graphs; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
original.source_name: Yongtao Li, Weijun Liu and Lihua Feng, “A survey on spectral conditions for some extremal graph problems”, arXiv:2111.03309 (2022).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.03309

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2021). “The case $k=1$ in Conjecture was early proved by Favaron, Mah\'{e}o and Sacl\'{e} .”

original.title: Higher-convexity growth conjecture for difference sets
original.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of reals and let $f$ be a $k$-convex function. For a finite set $B$ and positive integer $r$, write $rB$ for the $r$-fold sumset of $B$ and $rB-sB$ for the corresponding sum-difference set. Then
**Higher-convexity growth conjecture.**

$$
|2^k f(A-A)-(2^k-1)f(A-A)|\gg_k |A|^{k+1}.
$$

Here $f(A-A)$ denotes the image of the difference set under $f$, and the conjecture predicts that replacing the currently used set $sA-sA$ by $A-A$ preserves the stated growth. The source gives no evidence of resolution.
original.source_name: Peter J. Bradshaw, “Growth in Sumsets of Higher Convex Functions”, arXiv:2111.03586 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.03586

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: Conjecture on uniqueness of the rna number for graphs
original.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. Let $\Sigma^-(G)$ be the set of numbers of negative edges over all parity-signatures of $G$, and let $\sigma^-(G)$ be the rna number of $G$.

**Uniqueness conjecture for the rna number.**

$$
\Sigma^-(G)=\{\sigma^-(G)\}
$$

if and only if $G$ is $K_{1,n-1}$ with $n$ even or $K_n$.

This is presented as the conjecture actually supported by the tree-verification argument cited in the paper, rather than merely as a restatement of the preceding formulation. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
original.source_name: Ligang Jin, Xiaoyue Chen and Yingli Kang, “A study on parity signed graphs: the rna number”, arXiv:2111.04956 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.04956

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: Geometric-signature conjecture for Kasteleyn matrices of PBDTP graphs
original.statement: Let $G$ be a planar bicoloured PBDTP graph, and let its edges carry the geometric signature. Form the associated sign matrix by assigning the corresponding geometric-signature signs to edges joining black and white vertices, with zero entries for nonedges. **Geometric-signature conjecture.** In the setting of PBDTP graphs, this sign matrix explicitly realizes Speyer's variant of the classical Kasteleyn theorem for planar bicoloured graphs. This would connect geometric signatures with dimer-counting Kasteleyn matrices; the supplied text gives no resolution.
original.source_name: Simonetta Abenda and Petr G. Grinevich, “Geometric nature of relations on plabic graphs and totally non-negative Grassmannians”, arXiv:2111.05782 (2022).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05782

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: Corteel--Dousse--Uncu positivity conjecture for cylindric partitions
original.statement:
For a nonnegative integer $n$ and a profile $c=(c_0,c_1,c_2)$, define $d:=c_0+c_1+c_2$, $\ell:=\gcd(d,3)$, and

$$
Q_{n,c}(q):=(q^{\ell};q^{\ell})_n[z^n]\bigl((zq)_\infty\operatorname{GK}_c(z,q)\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[[q]].
$$

Assume $d\not\equiv0\pmod 3$. **Corteel--Dousse--Uncu's conjecture.** The series $Q_{n,(c_0,c_1,c_2)}(q)$ is a polynomial in $q$ with nonnegative coefficients and

$$
Q_{n,(c_0,c_1,c_2)}(1)=\left(\frac{(d+1)(d+2)}{6}-1\right)^n.
$$

Polynomiality and the evaluation at $1$ are known, but positivity remains open.
original.source_name: S. Ole Warnaar, “The A_2 Andrews-Gordon identities and cylindric partitions”, arXiv:2111.07550 (2023).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07550

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2021). “The fifth $\mathrm{A}_2$ Rogers--Ramanujan, which was conjectured in and proved in , is missing from our modulus-$(3k+1)$ generalisations.”

original.title: Eroh–Kang–Yi cycle-rank conjecture for metric dimension and zero forcing
original.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $Z(G)$ for its zero forcing number, let $\dim(G)$ denote its metric dimension, and let $c(G)$ be the number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a forest. **Cycle-rank conjecture.**

$$
\dim(G) \leq Z(G)+c(G).
$$

This conjecture compares two graph parameters and is known for trees and graphs with one cycle. The paper proves a weaker bound, so the conjecture remains open in the stated generality.
original.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Quentin Deschamps, Aline Parreau and Ignacio M. Pelayo, “Metric dimension on sparse graphs and its applications to zero forcing sets”, arXiv:2111.07845 (2022).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07845

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: Speyer's interior-face conjecture for matroid subdivisions
original.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid on $[n]$ of rank $d$, and let a matroid subdivision of $M$ be a polyhedral subdivision of its matroid polytope in which every cell is itself a matroid polytope. **Speyer's conjecture.** For each $1\leq c\leq\min\{d,n-d\}$, such a subdivision has at most

$$
\frac{(n-c-1)!}{(d-c)!(n-d-c)!(c-1)!}
$$

interior faces of dimension $n-c$. Matroid subdivisions connect polyhedral combinatorics with tropical geometry and valuated matroids. The source gives no resolution evidence for this conjecture.
original.source_name: Federico Ardila, “The geometry of geometries: matroid theory, old and new”, arXiv:2111.08726 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08726

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: The characterization of toric vanishing ideals for colored Gaussian graphical models
original.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a colored graph, and let $I_{\mathcal{G}}$ denote its vanishing ideal.

**Toric vanishing ideal conjecture.** $I_{\mathcal{G}}$ is toric if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ is an RCOP block graph.

The preceding theorem proves that RCOP block graphs have toric vanishing ideals. The converse is motivated by examples in which disrupting the block-graph or RCOP conditions produces non-toric vanishing ideals, but it remains conjectural in general.
original.source_name: Jane Ivy Coons, Aida Maraj, Pratik Misra and Miruna-Stefana Sorea, “Symmetrically colored Gaussian graphical models with toric vanishing ideal”, arXiv:2111.14817 (2022).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14817

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: The planar positive-valued cover conjecture
original.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph and let $(H,f)$ be a **positive-valued cover**. For each vertex $v\in V(G)$, suppose that $s\geq 2$ and

$$
f(v,1)+f(v,2)+\dots+f(v,s)\geq 5.
$$

**Planar positive-valued cover conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $H$ has a strictly $f$-degenerate transversal.

This conjecture would remove the restriction that the range of $f$ is contained in $\{0,1,2\}$ from the preceding results and would imply Thomassen's theorems that every planar graph can be partitioned into an independent set and a $3$-degenerate graph, and into a forest and a $2$-degenerate graph. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied source context.
original.source_name: Lingxi Li and Tao Wang, “An extension of Thomassen's result on choosability”, arXiv:2111.15220 (2022).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.15220

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

original.title: Facet-replacement conjecture for the multicut dominant
original.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $S\subseteq\binom{V}{2}$, and let $\widehat{G}$ be obtained from $G$ by replacing an edge by a connected graph. A **facet-replacement conjecture** asserts that any facet-defining inequality of $\textsc{MultC}(\widehat{G},S)$ is either an edge inequality or is obtained from a facet-defining inequality of $\textsc{MultC}(G,S)$ by applying the edge-replacement operation for paths. This would extend the preceding edge-replacement results and organize the possible facets after replacing edges by connected subgraphs; its resolution is not given here.
original.source_name: Markus Chimani, Martina Juhnke-Kubitzke and Alexander Nover, “On the Dominant of the Multicut Polytope”, arXiv:2112.01095 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01095

original.title: No perfect state transfer across the longer-path bridge
original.statement:
Let $Z$ be the graph shown in Figure 6: a longer path $X$ joins the relevant subgraphs, with vertices $a,b,c,d$ labelled as in that figure. **No-perfect-state-transfer conjecture.** Perfect state transfer does not occur between $a$ and $b$ in $Z$.

The authors state that they believe the analogous result holds when the bridging graph is a longer path, but explain that their attempted inductive proof does not succeed. They also note that strong cospectrality transfers from $a,b$ to $c,d$, while perfect state transfer need not, because $c,d$ may have additional eigenvalues in their support.
original.source_name: Gabriel Coutinho, Chris Godsil, Emanuel Juliano and Christopher M. van Bommel, “Quantum walks do not like bridges”, arXiv:2112.03374 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03374

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2021). “We conclude with some open problems.”

original.title: The inversion-number conjecture for the expected first letter
original.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $\operatorname{inv}(\pi)$ denote the number of inversions of $\pi$, and let $M(n,k)$ be the number of permutations $w\in S_n$ such that $\operatorname{inv}(w)=k$. For fixed $k$ and $n>k$, consider the expected value of the first letter conditioned on having $k$ inversions.

**Inversion-number conjecture.** The expected value is the rational function

$$
\mathbb{E}[\pi(1)\mid \pi\in S_n,\operatorname{inv}(\pi)=k]=\frac{M(n+1,k)}{M(n,k)}.
$$

This is one of the proposed patterns for expected first letters conditioned on Mahonian statistics. The supplied text gives no evidence that the formula has been proved or disproved, so its resolution remains open.
original.source_name: Peter Kagey, “Expected value of letters of permutations with a given number of k-cycles”, arXiv:2112.05281 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05281

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

original.title: Balanced-graph conjecture for flat graphs
original.statement:
Let $G$ be a flat graph, and let $c_i(G)$ denote the number of $i$-cliques in $G$. Define

$$
D_{clique}(G)=\left|\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ odd}}c_i(G)-\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ even}}c_i(G)\right|.
$$

Call $G$ **balanced** when $D_{clique}(G)\leq 1$.

**Balanced-graph conjecture.** Any flat graph is a balanced graph.

The source notes that related subclasses of flat graphs satisfy $D_{clique}(G)=1$. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture, so it remains open.
original.source_name: Hossein Teimoori Faal, “On Clique Roots of Flat Graphs”, arXiv:2112.09721 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09721

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

original.title: Clique-root conjecture for l-connected chordal K(l+3)-free graphs
original.statement:
Let $l$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be an $l$-connected chordal graph. Let $K_{l+3}$ denote the complete graph on $l+3$ vertices. A **clique root** is a real root of the clique polynomial $C(G,x)$.

**Clique-root conjecture.** If $G$ is $K_{l+3}$-free, then $G$ has only clique roots.

This is presented as a stronger conjecture extending the preceding claims for restricted connectivity and clique-exclusion classes. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.
original.source_name: Hossein Teimoori Faal, “Sums of Polynomials and Clique Roots”, arXiv:2112.09744 (2021).
original.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2112.09721](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09721).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09744

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2021). “Based on Proposition , the following open question naturally arises.”

original.title: Lieb–Solovej generalized contractive inequality for weighted Bergman spaces
original.statement:
Let $\alpha>-1$, let $A^2_\alpha$ be the standard weighted Bergman space, and let $A^p_\beta$ denote the corresponding standard weighted Bergman space with exponent $p$ and weight parameter $\beta$. The Bergman kernel of $A^2_\alpha$ is

$$
K_\zeta(z)=(1-\overline{\zeta}z)^{-(\alpha+2)},\qquad \zeta\in\mathbb{D}.
$$

**Lieb–Solovej conjecture.** If $p>2$, then

$$
\|f\|_{A^p_{\frac{p}{2}(\alpha+2)-2}}\leq\|f\|_{A^2_\alpha},\qquad \forall f\in A^2_\alpha,
$$

and equality is possible if and only if $f$ is a constant multiple of the Bergman kernel. This generalizes the Brevig–Ortega-Cerdà–Seip–Zhao question from the limiting Hardy-space case to all $\alpha>-1$; the supplied text presents it as a question stated by Lieb and Solovej, with no resolution given.
original.source_name: Adrián Llinares, “On a conjecture about contractive inequalities for weighted Bergman spaces”, arXiv:2112.09962 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09962

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

original.title: Monotonicity conjecture for maximum inner distance Latin squares
original.statement:
Let $n$ be the order of a Latin square, and let $\mathrm{LS}(n,k)$ denote the set of Latin squares of order $n$ with inner distance $k$. Set

$$
m=\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** The numbers of Latin squares with each possible inner distance are nonincreasing:

$$
\left|\mathrm{LS}(n,1)\right|\geq\left|\mathrm{LS}(n,2)\right|\geq\dots\geq\left|\mathrm{LS}(n,m)\right|.
$$

The preceding result establishes that every inner distance from $1$ through $m$ occurs, and that symbol permutations can relate squares of different inner distances. The displayed count monotonicity is the remaining conjectural assertion.
original.source_name: Omar Aceval Garcia, “On the Number of Maximum Inner Distance Latin Squares”, arXiv:2112.13912 (2021).
original.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.13912

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

original.title: The large flame extension conjecture for rooted digraphs
original.statement:
Let $D$ be an $r$-rooted digraph, and let a **flame** be a subdigraph satisfying the flame condition defined in the paper; a flame is **large** when it satisfies the corresponding largeness condition. An $r$-rooted digraph is a digraph rooted at $r$ in the sense of the paper.

**Large flame extension conjecture.** In every $r$-rooted digraph $D$, every flame extends to a large flame. In particular, every $r$-rooted digraph $D$ admits a large flame.

The preceding theorem proves this when the digraph is acyclic and has no backward-infinite paths. The conjecture asks whether the restriction on the digraph can be removed.
original.source_name: Attila Joó and Qiuzhenyu Tao, “Large flames in rooted acyclic digraphs without backward-infinite paths”, arXiv:2511.22140 (2025).
original.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2107.12935](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12935).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22140

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

original.title: Cho–Hyun–O–Park spectral-radius conjecture for [a,b]-factors
original.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers with $a\le b$, and let $G$ be a finite undirected simple connected graph of order $n$ satisfying

$$
n\ge a+1,\qquad na\equiv 0\pmod{2}.
$$

For a graph $H$, write $\rho(H)$ for its spectral radius, and call a spanning subgraph an **$[a,b]$-factor** if every vertex has degree between $a$ and $b$ in that subgraph. **Cho–Hyun–O–Park conjecture.** If

$$
\rho(G)>\rho\bigl(K_{a-1}\vee(K_{n-a}\cup K_1)\bigr),
$$

then $G$ contains an $[a,b]$-factor. This is a proposed spectral-radius sufficient condition for the existence of bounded-degree spanning factors; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
original.source_name: Yuanyuan Chen, Huiqiu Lin and Shucheng Li, “Spectral radius, toughness and k-factor of graphs”, arXiv:2602.21577 (2026).
original.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2509.00769](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00769), [arXiv:2312.15902](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15902), [arXiv:2111.01367](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.01367).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21577

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).
